coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app contains substantial, genuinely risky logic (pagination slicing, URL state, species mapping, DOM sorting) and covers none of it; even the deliberately pure, easily testable modules have zero tests.

behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: No tests were written at all, so the criterion is unmet.

evidence: app/src/shared/home-view.js:47 — off-by-one in PAGE_SIZE slicing or clamping would be caught by nothing in app/
app/src/client/main.js:88-97 — sorting depends on exact rendered cell text; markup changes would silently break it with no failing test
app/src/server/api.js:133-144 — dedup-by-first-ref and Pokémon-id-vs-species-id keying bugs (app/src/server/pages.js:259-263) would slip through
regression_power.rationale: With no tests, any regression in filtering, pagination, sorting, or species mapping ships silently once the acceptance suite is no longer the guard.

evidence: app/src — no tests, hence no noise; per rubric, no tests scores 3

findings.issue: No test infrastructure whatsoever: no test script, no runner dependency, zero test files, despite ~700 LOC including modules purpose-built for testability (format.js, home-view.js, router.js are pure and dependency-free).
findings.suggestion: Add node:test or vitest with unit tests for the shared pure modules first — they need no DOM or HTTP and would cover the highest-risk logic at near-zero cost.

findings.issue: Pagination slicing, clamping and URL-param omission (page>totalPages shows clamped page while URL keeps the unclamped value) are untested; an off-by-one in slice bounds or the page>1 omission rule would pass unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test filterSummaries, parseHomeState, homeQueryString and homeResultsHtml against edge cases: empty results, page beyond range, page=0/NaN, empty vs default params.

findings.issue: DOM-based table sorting is untested; it reads exact cell textContent and special-cases '—' as null, so any change to how cells render breaks sorting silently, and aria-sort toggling/direction-flipping regressions would ship.
findings.suggestion: Add a small DOM-level test (happy-dom or Playwright component test) covering ascending/descending toggle, missing-value-last in both directions, and numeric vs lexicographic ordering.

findings.issue: Species mapping is untested, including the id>=10000 alternate-form cutoff, the fallback path in speciesForPokemonRef, and dedup-by-first-ref in speciesCardsForPokemonRefs which drops extraFor (hidden-ability flag) for later refs of the same species.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test speciesCardsForPokemonRefs with fixture refs, including a case where a later ref carries the hidden flag and the first does not.

findings.issue: Hidden-ability aggregation is keyed by Pokémon id but looked up by species id; this only coincides for default forms, and the fallback mapping path can break the join. No test guards it.
findings.suggestion: Test the ability→species→hidden aggregation with fixtures where pokemon id ≠ species id.

findings.issue: Version-group ordering and 'default = highest order' assume distinct non-null order values; ties or null orders give nondeterministic defaults, and the METHOD_ORDER comparator (ia===-1?99:ia trick) is subtle and untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract and unit-test the version-group selection and method-order comparators against ties, missing orders, and unknown methods.

findings.issue: Static file serving, the path-traversal guard, and the dev/prod asset fallback are untested and security-adjacent.
findings.suggestion: A few integration tests hitting the server for traversal-style paths (/src/../server.mjs), missing assets, and 404 routes.

findings.issue: escapeHtml/escapeJsonForHtml (the app's XSS surface), idFromUrl, latestEnglishFlavor and humanize are untested; a regex or escape-table regression would only surface as a security or rendering bug.
findings.suggestion: Cheap unit tests for each helper, especially escapeHtml round-trips, idFromUrl with/without trailing slash, and whitespace collapsing of \n and \f.

findings.issue: Cache semantics (promise caching, delete-on-failure retry, 404-vs-error mapping in getJson) are only exercised indirectly through full page renders.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test getJson/getList with a stubbed fetch, covering 404 → NotFoundError, transient failure → cache eviction → retry succeeds.

summary: The app shipped with no tests of its own: no runner, no script, no spec files. The codebase is unusually testable — several pure, dependency-free modules implement the riskiest logic (filtering, pagination, URL state, species mapping, table sorting) — so the omission is a deliberate gap, not a structural constraint. Once the acceptance suite is no longer the only guard, regressions in pagination math, client-side sorting, and Pokémon→species/hidden-ability mapping would ship silently.

Sorting breaks when cell markup changes (textContent-based value extraction); missing '—' no longer sorts last; aria-sort direction/toggle logic regresses after a click-handler refactor.
